question: Should OpenClaw core accept this default-off continuation substrate with model-elected work, delegation, compaction, durable return delivery, and trusted internal cross-session enrichment?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it changes core agent autonomy, persisted session state, plugin SDK boundaries, and security-sensitive event delivery, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and trust model.

options.title: Sponsor after proof and security review
options.body: Proceed only after conflicts are resolved, exact-head live proof covers continue_work, continue_delegate, and accepted request_compaction, and core/security owners approve the trust and session-state model.

options.title: Ask for a staged split
options.body: Require a smaller sequence that lands the core substrate, security/SDK boundary, and user-facing tooling separately with focused proof for each stage.

options.title: Pause or close as too broad
options.body: Decline the broad core feature for now and ask for narrower issues or plugin/skill-level experiments before reopening core work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after proof and security review
recommendation.body: Proceed only after conflicts are resolved, exact-head live proof covers continue_work, continue_delegate, and accepted request_compaction, and core/security owners approve the trust and session-state model.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged history spans the core agent, TaskFlow, and system-event surfaces that would own the product-direction decision.
